pull.title: BIP32: specify the maximum depth of 255
pull.body:
BIP32 serializes the depth as one byte but does not say what happens when deriving past depth 255. Bitcoin Core refuses, while several libraries let the depth overflow (bitcoin/bitcoin#32201). In that issue @sipa said a hard limit is better for interoperability and that he would add a note to the BIP: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32201#issuecomment-3847331033

I added that note: deriving a child of a depth-255 key must fail. I also added test vector 6, with the keys at depth 255 on the chain m/0/0/.../0 (255 levels). I checked them with Bitcoin Core 31.1 and btclib-wallet, and both refuse to derive any child of them.

I left out the derivation path parsing rules raised in bitcoin/bitcoin#35306. I am happy to add them here if reviewers prefer.

*Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

BIP32: use a Changelog section, write out the depth-255 chain

comments.body:
Thank you, done in baa9dffa.

The block before the preamble is gone. BIP 32 now has a `==Changelog==` section at the end and a `Version: 2.1.0` header. The six historic entries keep their text and dates, in the format of BIP 3.

The version numbers are a proposal. They follow BIP 3, one version per entry, with the oldest entry as 1.0.0, as in BIP 85. If BIP 32 was still a draft in April 2013, the 2013 entries could be 0.x.y instead, as in BIP 8 and BIP 127:

* 1.0.0 (2013-04-16) private derivation for hardened indexes
* 2.0.0 (2013-04-30) addition instead of multiplication (incompatible, so major)
* 2.0.1 (2013-05-25) test vectors
* 2.0.2 (2014-01-15) hardened terminology and conversion functions
* 2.0.3 (2017-02-24) test vectors
* 2.0.4 (2020-11-04) test vectors
* 2.1.0 (this change) maximum depth, backward-compatible, so minor

@sipa, could you confirm or correct these numbers?

comments.body:
Thank you, done in baa9dffa.

The chain is now written out as the literal path, with all 255 levels. I counted the `/0` components with a script (255), and checked that the xpub and xprv decode to depth 255 and match a derivation from the seed along that path, both from the private key and from the master public key.

The note "(255 levels)" is now a comment above the path. The sentence that deriving any child must fail stays visible.
